What was the immediate cause for the launch of the Swadeshi Movement?
o: The partition of Bengal done by Lord Curzon.
A sentence of eighteen months rigorous imprisonment imposed on Lokmanya Tilak.
The arrest and deportation of Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh, and passing of the Punjab Colonisation Bill.
Death sentence pronounced on the Chapekar brothers.
x: The Swadeshi Movement was launched in 1905 as a direct response to the Partition of Bengal announced by Lord Curzon. The partition was perceived as a deliberate attempt to divide Bengal on communal lines and weaken the nationalist movement. The movement promoted self-reliance (Swadeshi) by boycotting foreign goods and using Indian products, uniting diverse groups in a nationwide movement for self-rule, and leading to a significant cultural and political awakening.

s: Who was the first to suggest the boycott of British goods in Bengal?

In his opinion, the manufacturing of British goods should be abolished. s: Vande Mataram became the theme song of the Indian National Movement during –
x: During Swadeshi Movement, the actual day of partition, October 16, 1905 A.D., was declared a day of mourning throughout Bengal and the hearths in the houses were kept unlit. People tied rakhis on each other wrists as a symbol of brotherhood. In Calcutta, most of the offices were kept closed, and a strike was observed in some jute mills and railway workshops. The music of this song is inspired by the melody of the Hymn ‘Ami Kothay Pabo Tare’ written by Gagan Harkara. Bangladesh adopted the first 10 lines of this song as its National Anthem. Syed Ali Ahsan translated the song into English. It is noteworthy that Rabindranath Tagore wrote the National Anthem of India ‘Jana Gana Mana’. He is the only poet in the world whose compositions have been adopted as the national anthem of the two countries.
